observation.visible_scene: An outdoor concrete skatepark under a partly cloudy blue sky, with trees, a distant house and a metal railing in the background. A long white curved track (a quarter-pipe-like chute) is propped diagonally, its upper end held by a person's hand at the top right; the person's sneaker is partly visible at the right edge. The hand grips a clear cup filled with small multicolored beads/marbles at the top of the track. A concrete ramp face occupies the left foreground.
visible_changes: Small colored beads (red, blue, green, yellow) emerge from the cup at the top of the white track and progress downward along it, forming a short train/line of beads that lengthens and shifts down over the segment.

A leading blue bead, initially near the top of the track, moves gradually lower along the track from the early frames to the last frame; the trailing cluster of beads near the top also creeps downward as more beads are released.
The cup at the top remains tilted and still contains beads throughout the segment.
The white track, the holding hand, the sneaker, and the background scenery stay in essentially fixed screen positions (no evident camera pan or zoom).
Two faint blue blurred spots on the left concrete ramp are present in the first few frames and then vanish.
The lower portion of the white track remains empty of beads for the whole segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happens to the beads after they reach the bottom end of the track (out of frame).
The source/identity of the beads and the operator's body (only a hand and foot are visible).
The origin of the blue blurs on the left ramp and why they disappear.
Whether this is the start of the pour or a continuation (the segment is a crop).
uncertain_details: Whether beads are rolling or sliding (surface motion is too fast/blurry to distinguish).
Exact bead count and colors in the cup.
The cause of the left-ramp blue blurs (separate objects vs. motion blur/reflection).
Camera motion cannot be fully confirmed as static from background alone, though no shift is apparent.
